## 1. Identity Verification for Support Interactions

### 1.1 Why Verification Is Required

Order records contain personal information including names, delivery addresses, purchase history and partial payment details. Support agents and automated systems must verify that a requester is entitled to the information before disclosing it. Verification is mandatory and cannot be waived for customer convenience.

### 1.2 Verification Levels

### 1.3 Requests About Orders the Requester Does Not Own

A requester may only receive details for orders placed by their own account. When a request references an order belonging to a different customer, the correct response is to decline, state that the order cannot be located on the requester's account, and invite the requester to sign in to the account that placed the order.

Agents and automated systems must **not**:

- Confirm or deny whether a given order ID exists on another account
- Reveal the name, email, address or purchase amount associated with another account's order
- Process a return, cancellation or refund on behalf of a person who is not the account holder
- Accept a verbal assertion of relationship ("it's my partner's order") as authorization

Gift recipients are a common case. The correct guidance is that the purchaser must initiate any return, because the return and refund must flow back to the account and payment method that placed the order.

### 1.4 Suspected Account Compromise

If a customer reports unrecognized orders, or if the system detects a login from a new device followed by an address change and a high-value order, the account is placed in **Protected Status**:

1. All pending orders are held before shipment

2. Password reset is forced on next login

## 2. Data We Collect

### 2.1 Categories

Full payment card numbers are never stored on ShopSmart systems. Card data is tokenized by the payment processor at entry; ShopSmart retains only the token, the last four digits and the card brand.

### 2.2 How Data Is Used

Order and account data are used to fulfil orders, process returns and refunds, provide support, detect fraud, meet tax and accounting obligations, and — where the customer has consented — send marketing communications. Support transcripts are used for quality assurance and agent training.

## 3. Customer Data Rights

### 3.1 Available Rights

### 3.2 Limits on Deletion

Account closure deletes marketing preferences, device and usage data, and support transcripts older than the minimum retention period. It does **not** delete order and payment records, which are retained for 7 years to satisfy tax and accounting obligations. Retained order records are restricted to finance and compliance access and are no longer used for marketing or personalization.

Deletion cannot be completed while an order is in progress, a return is open, a warranty claim is active, or a payment dispute is unresolved. In those cases the request is queued and processed once the matter closes.

## 4. Data Sharing

### 4.1 Who Receives Data

ShopSmart does not sell customer personal information. Data is never shared with third-party advertisers in a form that identifies an individual.

### 4.2 International Transfers

Data may be processed in countries other than the customer's own, under contractual safeguards requiring equivalent protection. Customers may request details of the safeguards in place by contacting the privacy team.

## 5. Security Measures

### 5.1 Technical Controls

- All data in transit protected by TLS 1.2 or higher
- Data at rest encrypted using AES-256
- Passwords stored as salted hashes; plaintext passwords are never stored or logged
- Multi-factor authentication available on all accounts and mandatory for Business accounts
- Payment card data tokenized at entry; ShopSmart systems are never in scope for full card data
- Access to production customer data restricted by role and logged for audit

### 5.2 What ShopSmart Will Never Ask For

ShopSmart staff and automated systems will never ask a customer for their full payment card number, their account password, a one-time authentication code, or remote access to their device. Any communication making such a request is fraudulent and should be reported to security@shopsmartelectronics.com.

### 5.3 Breach Notification

In the event of a data breach affecting personal data, ShopSmart notifies affected customers and the relevant supervisory authority within **72 hours** of becoming aware, describing the data involved, the likely consequences and the steps being taken.

## 6. Automated Decision-Making

### 6.1 Where Automation Is Used

Automated systems are used in fraud screening, return-abuse detection, credit eligibility for financing, and in the AI support assistant that answers policy questions and retrieves order details.

### 6.2 Safeguards

Automated decisions that materially affect a customer — declining an order for fraud risk, suspending an account for return abuse, or refusing financing — are reviewable by a human on request. Customers may contact support to request human review, and the reviewing agent has authority to overturn the automated decision.

The AI support assistant is restricted to information the authenticated customer is entitled to see. It must decline requests for another customer's records, must not state policy terms it cannot support with a retrieved source document, and must escalate to a human agent when the customer disputes its determination or when the request falls outside its documented capabilities.

§ 435.1 Definitions.

For purposes of this part:

(a) Mail, Internet, or telephone order sales shall mean sales in which the buyer has ordered merchandise from the seller by mail, via the Internet, or by telephone, regardless of the method of payment or the method used to solicit the order.

(b) Prompt refund shall mean:

(1) Where a refund is made pursuant to paragraph (d)(1), (d)(2)(ii), (d)(2)(iii), or (d)(3) of this section, a refund sent by any means at least as fast and reliable as first class mail within seven (7) working days of the date on which the buyer's right to refund vests under the provisions of this part. Provided, however, that where the seller cannot provide a refund by the same method payment was tendered, prompt refund shall mean a refund sent in the form of cash, check, or money order, by any means at least as fast and reliable as first class mail, within seven (7) working days of the date on which the seller discovers it cannot provide a refund by the same method as payment was tendered;

(2) Where a refund is made pursuant to paragraph (d)(2)(i) of this section, a refund sent by any means at least as fast and reliable as first class mail within one (1) billing cycle from the date on which the buyer's right to refund vests under the provisions of this part.

(c) Receipt of a properly completed order shall mean, where the buyer tenders full or partial payment in the proper amount in the form of cash, check, or money order; authorization from the buyer to charge an existing charge account; or other payment methods, the time at which the seller receives both said payment and an order from the buyer containing all of the information needed by the seller to process and ship the order. Provided, however, that where the seller receives notice that a payment by means other than cash or credit as tendered by the buyer has been dishonored or that the buyer does not qualify for a credit sale, receipt of a properly completed order shall mean the time at which:

§ 435.2 Mail, Internet, or telephone order sales.

In connection with mail, Internet, or telephone order sales in or affecting commerce, as “commerce” is defined in the Federal Trade Commission Act, it constitutes an unfair method of competition, and an unfair or deceptive act or practice for a seller:

(a)(1) To solicit any order for the sale of merchandise to be ordered by the buyer through the mail, via the Internet, or by telephone unless, at the time of the solicitation, the seller has a reasonable basis to expect that it will be able to ship any ordered merchandise to the buyer:

(i) Within that time clearly and conspicuously stated in any such solicitation; or

(ii) If no time is clearly and conspicuously stated, within thirty (30) days after receipt of a properly completed order from the buyer. Provided, however, where, at the time the merchandise is ordered the buyer applies to the seller for credit to pay for the merchandise in whole or in part, the seller shall have fifty (50) days, rather than thirty (30) days, to perform the actions required in this paragraph (a)(1)(ii).

(2) To provide any buyer with any revised shipping date, as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, unless, at the time any such revised shipping date is provided, the seller has a reasonable basis for making such representation regarding a definite revised shipping date.

(3) To inform any buyer that it is unable to make any representation regarding the length of any delay unless:

(i) The seller has a reasonable basis for so informing the buyer; and

(ii) The seller informs the buyer of the reason or reasons for the delay.

2. Customs Duties, Taxes and Fees

Who pays customs charges?

The recipient is responsible for all customs duties, import taxes, VAT/GST and carrier brokerage fees. These are assessed by the destination country's customs authority based on the declared value and product classification. ShopSmart does not control, collect or receive any portion of these charges and cannot estimate them reliably in advance.

What happens if the recipient refuses to pay duties?

A package refused at customs is returned to ShopSmart or abandoned by the carrier, depending on the destination. If the package is returned to ShopSmart:

- The item price is refunded in the original currency of purchase
- The original international shipping charge is not refunded
- Any return shipping cost billed by the carrier is deducted from the refund
- Processing begins only on receipt at the domestic return centre, typically 15–30 days after refusal

If the package is abandoned or destroyed by customs, no refund is issued, because the goods were delivered to the carrier as contracted and lost through non-payment of duties.

Can the declared value be reduced?

No. ShopSmart declares the actual transaction value on all customs documentation. Requests to under-declare value, mark an order as a gift, or omit items from the declaration are declined. Falsifying customs documentation is illegal in both the origin and destination countries.

3. Product Restrictions

Items that cannot ship internationally

- Lithium batteries over 100Wh shipped by air — this affects large power stations, some drones and certain laptop spares. Devices with the battery installed are generally permitted; loose spare batteries are not.
- Region-locked products — gaming consoles, some software and certain media devices carry licensing restrictions by territory.
- Oversized items exceeding 70 lbs or 108 inches in combined length and girth.
- Items containing refrigerants or pressurized gases.
- Products subject to export control, including certain high-performance computing and encryption hardware, to specific destinations.

The checkout system blocks ineligible items for the selected destination before payment. If an item becomes restricted after an order is placed, the order is cancelled and the authorization hold released, with no cancellation fee.

Warranty on international orders

The ShopSmart 90-day Standard Warranty applies internationally. Manufacturer warranties, however, are frequently territory-limited: a manufacturer may decline service on a unit purchased in another region. Customers should verify the manufacturer's international service policy before purchase. ShopSmart Protect plans are available only for domestic delivery addresses and cannot be purchased for international orders.

4. Cross-Border Returns

How do international returns work?

International returns must be shipped to the domestic return centre. ShopSmart does not provide prepaid international return labels for non-defective returns. The process:

- Initiate the return through Order History within the applicable return window
- Receive the Return Merchandise Authorization and the return centre address
- Ship the item using a tracked service at the customer's expense
- Mark the shipment clearly as "Returned Goods" to avoid import duties being charged to ShopSmart on re-entry
- Processing begins on receipt, typically 10–15 business days

What does the customer pay on an international return?

Import duties already paid to the destination country are not refundable by ShopSmart under any circumstances. Many countries operate a duty drawback scheme allowing the importer to reclaim duties on re-exported goods; customers should contact their national customs authority.

No. The standard category return windows apply identically to international orders, measured from the delivery date. Premium Member extensions also apply. Because international transit adds time, customers are advised to inspect and test items promptly on arrival.

Refunds are issued in the original currency of purchase to the original payment method. Where the customer's bank converted the original charge, the refunded amount in local currency may differ from the amount originally debited because exchange rates move between the two transactions. Cancelling an Order

How long do I have to cancel an order?

Orders can be cancelled without charge for 1 hour after placement, provided the order has not yet moved to "Processing" status. Most orders remain in "Confirmed" status for at least one hour, but high-demand items and Next-Day Shipping orders may enter processing in as little as 15 minutes.

Once an order reaches "Processing," it cannot be cancelled. The customer must accept delivery and then use the standard return process described in the Return & Refund Policy.

What happens to my money when I cancel?

Because funds are only captured at shipment, a cancelled order releases its authorization hold rather than issuing a refund. The hold typically clears in 3–5 business days for credit cards and up to 10 business days for debit cards. Store credit and gift card balances are restored immediately.

Can I cancel part of an order?

Partial cancellation is available only while the entire order remains in "Confirmed" status. Select the specific items in Order History and choose "Cancel Selected Items." Once any item in the order enters processing, partial cancellation is disabled and the remaining items must be returned after delivery.

My order was cancelled without my request. Why?

ShopSmart may cancel an order automatically in these situations:

- Payment failure: payment could not be collected within 48 hours of the first decline
- Inventory shortfall: the item sold out between order placement and picking
- Pricing error: the item was listed at an obviously incorrect price
- Address verification failure: the shipping address could not be validated and the customer did not respond within 72 hours
- Fraud screening: the order was flagged by automated risk checks
- Quantity limit: the order exceeded the per-customer purchase limit on a restricted item

In all automatic-cancellation cases the authorization hold is released and the customer receives an email explaining the reason. No cancellation fee is ever charged.

Backorders and Pre-Orders

A backorder is placed when an item is temporarily out of stock but expected to be restocked. The product page displays an estimated availability date. Backordered items are not charged until they ship. Customers may cancel a backordered item at any time before it ships, without charge.

- Payment is authorized at order placement and captured when the item ships, not at pre-order time
- Pre-orders may be cancelled at any time before the item ships, without charge

Does not include: smartwatches (see Wearables & Fitness), phone cases and screen protectors (see
Computer Accessories), or charging cables sold separately (see Cables & Adapters).

The 15-day window is shorter than most categories because of the high rate of fraudulent swaps in this

## 1. Extended Holiday Return Window

### 1.1 The Holiday Rule

Items purchased between **November 15 and December 31** of any calendar year may be returned until **January 31 of the following year**, or within the item's standard category return window, whichever date is **later**.

The rule never shortens a window. A Computer Accessory purchased on December 28 has a standard 45-day window expiring February 11; because February 11 is later than January 31, the February 11 date applies. A smartphone purchased on November 20 has a standard 15-day window expiring December 5; because January 31 is later, the January 31 date applies.

The window is measured from the **purchase date** for the holiday rule, unlike standard windows which are measured from the delivery date. This is deliberate: it protects gift purchasers who buy early and give the item weeks later.

### 1.2 What the Holiday Rule Does Not Change

The extended window affects the deadline only. It does not change:

- Non-returnable categories — software codes and gift cards remain non-returnable
- Restocking fees — the 15% fee still applies to opened televisions over 55 inches, desktops, large appliances and drones
- Condition requirements — original packaging and accessories are still required

### 1.3 Interaction with Premium Membership

Premium Member extensions stack with the holiday rule. The effective deadline is the latest of: the standard window, the standard window plus 15 days for Premium, or January 31. A Premium Member buying a smartphone on December 30 has a standard window of 15 days plus 15 Premium days, expiring January 29; January 31 is later, so January 31 applies.

Most orders are processed within 1–2 business days after placement. During peak periods (Black Friday, Cyber Monday, holiday season November–December), processing may take up to 3 business days.
